Once upon a time, a boy called Jack lived in a little cottage with his mum and their old cow, Milky-White.
They didn't have much, and the cupboard was nearly empty.
Here's our very last coin, Jack,
said Mother.
Can you take it to the market and get some seeds for our garden?
At the market, Jack met a funny little Peddler.
She had a cart full of seeds and a sleepy grey donkey.
I've got something even better than seeds,
said Peddler.
Five magic beans!
Plant them tonight, and peek out of your window in the morning.
So Jack gave her his coin, and she gave him the beans.
That evening, Jack showed his mum the five beans.
Only five beans?
said Mother, and she laughed.
Well, beans are seeds too.
Let's plant them and see!
So they planted the beans under the kitchen window: one, two, three, four, five.
Milky-White watched over the fence.
In the morning, Jack and his mum ran out into the garden.
Wow, look at that!
said Jack.
A great big beanstalk had grown in the night.
It went up, up, up, right into the clouds!
Even Milky-White looked up.
Moo, moo, moo!
Then the leaves started to rustle.
Rustle, rustle, rustle!
Down the beanstalk, leaf by leaf, came a fluffy little hen with shiny golden feathers.
She hopped onto Jack's arm.
Cluck, cluck, cluck!
Hello, little hen,
Are you lost?
I think she lives up in the clouds,
Somebody up there must be missing her.
Mum, can I take her home?
Let's take her home together,
She tied a basket onto Jack's back and tucked the little hen inside.
Hold on with both hands, one step at a time,
Jack held on to the beanstalk with both hands, and Mother climbed right behind him.
Hold on with both hands, one step at a time, Mum,
Up, up, up they climbed, nice and slow, past the treetops and the birds, right into the soft white clouds.
The little hen peeked out of the basket.
At the top, a fluffy cloud road led to a great big castle.
Boom, boom, boom!
Out stomped a Giant with a big, round, friendly face.
Fee, fi, fo, fum! Hello, hello, everyone!
sang Giant, so loud that all the birds flew away.
Jack giggled and put his fingers in his ears.
So did Mother.
Then the Giant saw the little hen in Jack's basket.
Goldie!
said Giant.
My Goldie!
I've been looking for you everywhere!
Jack lifted Goldie out, and she fluttered up into the Giant's big hands.
Thank you, thank you!
His happy voice was so loud that the castle windows went rattle, rattle, rattle!
The Giant sat down on his castle step and let out a great big sigh.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
The sigh blew Jack's cap right off his head.
Oops, sorry!
said Giant, and he caught the cap between two fingers.
Everything about me is too big and too loud.
When I say hello, the birds fly away, and nobody ever comes to play.
I can help!
Put a finger on your lips, like this, and sing as softly as a mouse.
The Giant put a finger on his lips.
whispered Giant.
This time the birds didn't fly away.
Two little bluebirds flew down and sat right on his shoulder.
Thank you, Jack,
You brought Goldie home, and you taught me to sing softly.
Goldie lays a golden egg every morning, and I'd like to share.
Very gently, the Giant put a shiny golden egg into Jack's basket.
Come and visit me every Sunday, both of you,
Jack and Mother waved bye-bye and started to climb down.
Down, down, down they went, nice and slow, with the golden egg safe and snug in his basket.
Bye-bye, my friends!
whispered Giant, and he waved from the edge of the cloud.
Jack and Mother stepped off the very last leaf.
The Peddler was waiting at the bottom.
Jack held up the golden egg.
It's a present from our new friend, the Giant,
Now we can buy seeds for the whole garden!
I told you they were magic beans,
said Peddler, and she gave a wink.
Mother gave Jack a great big hug.
That night, Mother tucked Jack into bed and kissed him goodnight.
From high up in the clouds came a soft little song.
Fee, fi, fo, fum! Goodnight, goodnight, everyone!
sang Giant, as softly as a mouse.
Night-night, Giant,
whispered Jack, and soon he was fast asleep.
And from that day on, Jack and the Giant were best friends.
